newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says will proceed warily in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says will proceed warily in Zaire.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd was likely to invest in strife-torn Zaire over the next few years but would do so with caution, Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said on Tuesday.
"We have a foot in Zaire and a few years down the road it may make sense to make investments there. But you can be sure we'll proceed in a cautious manner," he told a news conference.

Asked what Anglo's corporate view was on the situation in Zaire, Ogilvie Thompson said: "I don't know if we have a very clear corporate view. I don't know if the situation in Zaire is very clear. Zaire is not currently a coherent country."
"We have put in a bid for Kolwezi Copper and we're waiting to see how that is adjudicated. It depends on what Gecamines wants us to do," he added.
Anglo has put in a tender to retread the tailings from the copper mine which is owned by state mining company Gecamines.
